label: Dvin (siege, 624)
persian_force: The garrison of the Persian provincial capital of Armenia (no details in the sources).
iranian_note: A Sasanian provincial garrison in an Armenian city; its make-up is not recorded.
result_basis: Dvin, the capital of Persian Armenia, was taken and sacked.
sources: Sebeos 38; Howard-Johnston 2021; en.wikipedia Sack of Dvin (624)
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Ganzak
label: Ganzak
persian_force: Khosrow II's own army, about 40,000, with the royal guard (no breakdown in the sources).
iranian_note: The king's army in Atropatene, raised from the Iranian nobility and levies.
result_basis: Heraclius' Arab vanguard cut down Khosrow's guard, Khosrow fled south and his army dispersed.
sources: Sebeos 38; Theophanes AM 6114; Kaegi 2003, 122-126; en.wikipedia Battle of Ganzak
note: Heraclius then destroyed the fire temple of Adur Gushnasp. Also in Battles of the Romans.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Tigranakert
label: Tigranakert
place: near Tigranakert of Artsakh (near Aghdam), Azerbaijan
persian_force: Two of the three Persian armies sent against Heraclius, those of Shahraplakan and Shahin, 20,000-30,000 together (modern estimate).
iranian_note: Sasanian field armies operating in the Caucasus, probably with Albanian and Armenian levies.
result_basis: Heraclius routed first Shahraplakan's and then Shahin's army, taking Shahin's baggage train.
sources: Movses Dasxuranci 2.10; Theophanes AM 6115; Kaegi 2003, 128-129; en.wikipedia Battle of Aghdam (625)
note: en.wikipedia's 'Battle of Aghdam (625)' is this battle (against Shahin). Battles of the Romans has it as Tigranakert; one en.wikipedia article wrongly puts it at Tigranakert (Silvan).
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Aliovit (Archesh)
label: Aliovit (Archesh)
place: Archesh (Ercis), in the district of Aliovit, north of Lake Van, Turkey
persian_force: Shahrbaraz's army, part of it quartered in Archesh (no breakdown in the sources).
iranian_note: The Sasanian western field army under a Persian spahbed.
result_basis: Heraclius' night attack destroyed Shahrbaraz's camp and Shahrbaraz barely escaped.
sources: Theophanes AM 6115; Sebeos 38; Greatrex 1991, 206-208; en.wikipedia Battle of Archesh
note: Also in Battles of the Romans.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Sarus
label: Sarus
place: the bridge over the Sarus (Seyhan), near Adana, Turkey
persian_force: Shahrbaraz's army pursuing Heraclius (no breakdown in the sources).
iranian_note: The Sasanian western field army under a Persian spahbed.
result_basis: After the Persians ambushed the Roman vanguard, Heraclius led the rearguard across the bridge and turned the battle; the Romans held the field and Shahrbaraz withdrew in good order.
sources: Theophanes AM 6115; Kaegi 2003, 130-131; en.wikipedia Battle of Sarus
note: A nominal Roman victory: Shahrbaraz continued his advance. Also in Battles of the Romans.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Constantinople (siege)
label: Constantinople (siege)
place: Constantinople, the Golden Horn and the Bosporus, with the Persian army at Chalcedon, Turkey
commanders_b: the Avar khagan; Shahrbaraz and Kardarigan (Persian army at Chalcedon)
persian_force: Shahrbaraz's army encamped at Chalcedon, a whole corps acting as a unit; it could not cross the Bosporus (no breakdown in the sources).
iranian_note: The Sasanian western field army under a Persian spahbed.
strength_a: about 12,000 cavalry and the city militia
strength_b: about 80,000 Avars and Slavs, plus the Persian army
result_basis: The siege was abandoned after the Roman fleet destroyed the Slav boats, including those sent to ferry Persian troops across the Bosporus, on 7 August.
sources: Chronicon Paschale; Theodore Syncellus; George of Pisidia, Bellum Avaricum; en.wikipedia Siege of Constantinople (626)
note: The Persians fought chiefly as besiegers across the strait; the assault on the walls was by Avars and Slavs. Also in Battles of the Romans.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Lycus
label: Lycus
persian_force: Shahin's new army, raised by Khosrow in 625 from 'all the able men, including foreigners' (up to 50,000 according to Theophanes).
iranian_note: A newly levied Sasanian army; the levy of 625 is said to have included foreigners, so the share is uncertain.
result_basis: Theodore heavily defeated Shahin's army, which lost very heavily.
sources: Theophanes AM 6117; Kaegi 2003, 140-141; en.wikipedia Battle of the Lycus (626)
note: Shahin reportedly died soon after. Also in Battles of the Romans.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Derbent (627)
label: Derbent (627)
place: Derbent (Chor, the Caspian Gates), Dagestan, Russia
persian_force: The defenders of the Sasanian wall at Derbent, described as a lightly armed Albanian militia (Movses Dasxuranci).
iranian_note: The defenders are described as Albanians of the Sasanian province; a Persian garrison is not named.
result_basis: The Turks stormed the Sasanian fortifications at Derbent and went on to plunder Albania.
borderline: a Persian force is not attested; the defenders were the militia of Sasanian Albania
doubt: Borderline: a Persian force is not attested; the defenders were the militia of Sasanian Albania.
sources: Movses Dasxuranci 2.11; en.wikipedia Perso-Turkic war of 627-629
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Tiflis (siege)
label: Tiflis (siege)
war: Roman-Persian War of 602-628; Perso-Turkic war of 627-629
commanders_a: Heraclius, Tong Yabghu Qaghan, Bori Shad
commanders_b: Stephen I of Iberia (killed); a Persian governor; Shahraplakan sent 1,000 horse
persian_force: A Persian garrison with Iberian troops of Stephen I, reinforced by 1,000 cavalry sent by Shahraplakan.
iranian_note: A Persian garrison and 1,000 Persian horse alongside the Iberian prince's troops (Movses Dasxuranci).
strength_a: about 40,000 Turks left under Bori Shad, plus Heraclius' army
losses_b: the garrison killed; the Persian governor and the Iberian prince tortured to death
result_basis: After a first siege by the Romans and Turks failed in 627, the Turks returned and stormed the city in the winter of 627/628.
sources: Movses Dasxuranci 2.11-14; Theophanes AM 6117; en.wikipedia Siege of Tbilisi (627-628)
note: The Turks are called Khazars in several sources; Battles of the Romans lists Khazars. The first siege was abandoned; the place fell to the second.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Nineveh
label: Nineveh
place: near the ruins of Nineveh, by the Tigris (Mosul), Iraq
persian_force: Rhahzadh's army of about 12,000, with archers, in three divisions; 3,000 reinforcements arrived too late.
iranian_note: A Sasanian field army; its general Rhahzadh is said to have been Armenian.
result_basis: Rhahzadh was killed and his army lost about 6,000 men but stood near the field; it withdrew afterwards, and the Romans held the battlefield.
sources: Theophanes AM 6118; Nicephorus 14; Sebeos 38; en.wikipedia Battle of Nineveh (627)
note: The overthrow of Khosrow II (February 628) and the peace that followed are strategic consequences. Also in Battles of the Romans.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Edessa (siege, 630)
label: Edessa (siege, 630)
war: Roman-Persian War of 602-628 (evacuation after the peace)
persian_force: The Persian garrison of Edessa, which refused to evacuate after the peace of 628, reportedly encouraged by the city's Jews.
iranian_note: A Sasanian garrison left from the occupation of Mesopotamia.
result_basis: The Persian garrison, bombarded by Theodore's siege engines, agreed to leave and the city was handed over.
sources: Chronicle of 1234; Agapius; en.wikipedia Theodore (brother of Heraclius); Siege of Edessa (disambiguation, 630)
note: Theodore's troops then attacked the Jews of the city until Heraclius stopped them.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Ctesiphon (siege, 630)
label: Ctesiphon (siege, 630)
date: spring 630, the city taken 27 April 630 (629 in en.wikipedia's article title)
faction_a: Shahrbaraz (with the Parsig and Nimruzi factions)
persian_force: Shahrbaraz's 6,000 veterans of the western army, joined by the forces of the Parsig faction (Piruz Khosrow) and of the spahbed of Nimruz, against the troops of Ardashir III's regency in the capital.
iranian_note: Both sides were Sasanian forces led by Persian and Parthian nobles.
losses_b: Ardashir III and many nobles executed
result_basis: Ctesiphon fell to Shahrbaraz, who killed Ardashir III and took the throne.
sources: al-Tabari i.1061-1062; Chronicle of Seert; Pourshariati 2008, 180-183; en.wikipedia Siege of Ctesiphon (629)
note: Shahrbaraz failed at first and took the city with his allies' help. en.wikipedia's article is titled 'Siege of Ctesiphon (629)'; Pourshariati and the Shahrbaraz article give 27 April 630.
qbasis: Iranians on both sides (a civil war of the Iranian states)

name: Ctesiphon (631)
label: Ctesiphon (631)
persian_force: Rostam's army of the Pahlav (Parthian) nobility from Khorasan against the forces of Azarmidokht's regime under the Mihranid Siyavakhsh.
iranian_note: Both armies were Sasanian noble forces, Rostam's drawn from Khorasan.
result_basis: Rostam defeated Siyavakhsh's forces at Ctesiphon and took the city, deposing Azarmidokht.
borderline: no conventional battle name; the sources say only that Rostam defeated Azarmidokht's armies and took the capital
doubt: Borderline: no conventional battle name; the sources say only that Rostam defeated Azarmidokht's armies and took the capital.
sources: al-Tabari i.1064-1065; Pourshariati 2008, 204-209; en.wikipedia Sasanian civil war of 628-632
note: Rostam then blinded and killed Azarmidokht and restored Boran.
qbasis: Iranians on both sides (a civil war of the Iranian states)

name: Chains
label: Chains
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
persian_force: Hormozd's Sasanian frontier army of heavy troops, part of the infantry chained together, with many Christian Arab auxiliaries.
iranian_note: A Persian regular army with Christian Arab auxiliaries (al-Tabari after Sayf ibn Umar); the proportions are not given.
result_basis: The Persian wings broke and fled; the chained infantry could not escape and was cut down, leaving the field to Khalid.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan; en.wikipedia Battle of Chains
note: Khalid's battles of 633 are known mostly from Sayf ibn Umar, whose details (and some of the battles) are doubted by Donner and others.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: River
label: River
date: April 633 (12 Safar AH 12 according to Morony)
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
persian_force: Qarin's army sent from Ctesiphon, Persian regulars and new levies, joined by the survivors of the Chains.
iranian_note: A Persian relief army from the capital (al-Tabari); Qarin was of the Parthian Karen family.
result_basis: With its three commanders killed in single combat, the Persian army broke and fled to its boats on the river.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); Morony 1984; en.wikipedia Battle of the River
note: Called the battle of al-Madhar or al-Thani in the Arabic sources.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Hira
label: Hira
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
commanders_b: Iyas ibn Qabisa al-Ta'i, Abd al-Masih ibn Amr ibn Buqayla
persian_force: The Christian Arab townsmen of al-Hira (the Ibad) in the castles of the city, under its Sasanian-appointed governor; the Persian marzban Azadbeh had withdrawn.
iranian_note: The defenders were the Arab notables of the former Lakhmid capital, a Sasanian frontier city.
result_basis: After a short siege of its castles al-Hira surrendered and paid tribute.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12; Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan; en.wikipedia Battle of Hira
note: The castles named are al-Qasr al-Abyad, Qasr ibn Buqayla and Qasr al-Adasiyyin.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Ullais
label: Ullais
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: Ullais, between the Euphrates and the Khaseef, Iraq
commanders_a: Khalid ibn al-Walid, al-Muthanna ibn Haritha
commanders_b: Jaban; Abd al-Aswad al-Ijli (killed) and Abjar (Christian Arab wings)
persian_force: Imperial troops under Jaban in the centre, with Christian Arab contingents of Bakr ibn Wa'il and neighbouring tribes on both wings.
iranian_note: The Arabic sources put Persian regulars in the centre and Christian Arabs on both wings.
result_basis: After a long fight the Persian and Arab line broke and the fugitives were slaughtered (the 'River of Blood').
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); Crawford 2013; en.wikipedia Battle of Ullais
note: Bahman Jadhuyih, appointed to command, had returned to Ctesiphon.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Walaja
label: Walaja
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: al-Walaja, west of the Euphrates south of al-Hira, Iraq
commanders_a: Khalid ibn al-Walid, al-Muthanna ibn Haritha
commanders_b: Andarzaghar (died in the flight), Bahman Jadhuyih (did not arrive in time)
persian_force: Andarzaghar's army of garrison troops drawn from across the empire, with heavy cavalry on the wings and thousands of Christian Arabs of Bakr ibn Wa'il.
iranian_note: A Persian army with a large Christian Arab element (al-Tabari after Sayf ibn Umar).
result_basis: Khalid's hidden cavalry struck the Persian rear and Andarzaghar's army was destroyed.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Battle of Walaja
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: al-Anbar
label: al-Anbar
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
persian_force: Shirzad's Persian garrison in the fortress of al-Anbar.
iranian_note: A Persian garrison; the town's Arab population stayed on.
result_basis: After archery duels, an assault on the moat and a repulsed sortie, Shirzad surrendered al-Anbar and withdrew to Ctesiphon.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12; en.wikipedia Battle of al-Anbar
note: Called the 'Battle of the Eyes' for the Persians blinded by the Muslim archers.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Ayn al-Tamr
label: Ayn al-Tamr
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: Ayn al-Tamr (Shithatha), west of Karbala, Iraq
commanders_b: Mihran son of Bahram Chobin; Aqqa ibn Qays al-Namari (captured, executed)
persian_force: A field army of Christian Arabs (Namir, Taghlib, Iyad) under Aqqa, with Mihran's Persian regulars in the fortress.
iranian_note: The field army was mostly Christian Arab and the Persian regulars held the fort.
losses_b: the field army executed; the garrison killed
result_basis: Khalid captured Aqqa in the field battle, the Christian Arab army surrendered, and the fortress was then stormed and its Persian garrison killed.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12; Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan; en.wikipedia Battle of Ayn al-Tamr
note: A field battle followed by the storming of the fort; entered once.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Husayd
label: Husayd
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: Husayd, south-east of Ayn al-Tamr, Iraq
commanders_a: al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr al-Tamimi, Abu Layla
persian_force: One of two Persian field forces sent from Ctesiphon by Bahman Jadhuyih, joined by local Christian Arabs seeking revenge for Aqqa.
iranian_note: Persian field forces from the capital with some Christian Arab allies (al-Tabari after Sayf).
result_basis: Al-Qa'qa' attacked before the two Persian forces could unite; both commanders were killed and the survivors fled to Khanafis.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Battle of Husayd
note: The sources disagree on which commander was at Husayd and which at Khanafis.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Muzayyah
label: Muzayyah
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: al-Muzayyah (Mudayyah), north of Ayn al-Tamr, Iraq
commanders_b: Mahbudhan (Persian commander from Khanafis), Hudhayl ibn Imran (Christian Arabs)
persian_force: The Persian force withdrawn from Khanafis under Mahbudhan, with the Christian Arabs (Taghlib) of Hudhayl ibn Imran.
iranian_note: A Persian remnant joined to a Christian Arab army (al-Tabari after Sayf).
result_basis: Khalid's three-pronged night attack broke up the camp and thousands were killed; the rest fled in the dark.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Battle of Muzayyah
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Saniyy
label: Saniyy
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: al-Saniyy, on the edge of the Jazira, Iraq
persian_force: No Persian troops are attested; the camp was of Christian Arabs (Taghlib) raised for Bahman Jadhuyih's counter-offensive.
iranian_note: The sources describe only an Arab camp under Rabi'a ibn Bujayr.
result_basis: Khalid's night attack destroyed the Christian Arab camp and killed its leader.
borderline: no Persian troops attested; the Christian Arabs were Sasanian allies (en.wikipedia lists the Sasanian Empire as a belligerent)
doubt: Borderline: no Persian troops attested; the Christian Arabs were Sasanian allies (en.wikipedia lists the Sasanian Empire as a belligerent).
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Battle of Saniyy
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Zumail
label: Zumail
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
commanders_a: Khalid ibn al-Walid, Iyad ibn Ghanm, al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr
persian_force: No Persian troops are attested; an army of Christian Arabs (Taghlib) loyal to the Sasanians.
iranian_note: The sources describe only Christian Arab clans at Zumail.
result_basis: The Christian Arab army scattered under a three-sided night attack and was mostly destroyed in flight.
borderline: no Persian troops attested; the Christian Arabs were Sasanian allies
doubt: Borderline: no Persian troops attested; the Christian Arabs were Sasanian allies.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Battle of Zumail
note: Rabi'a ibn Bujayr appears as commander in some accounts, though he is said to have fallen at Saniyy.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Baqusiatha
label: Baqusiatha
persian_force: The army of Jalinus sent by Rostam to support Narsi.
iranian_note: A Persian field army raised by Rostam's regency.
result_basis: Jalinus' relief army, arriving too late for Kaskar, was defeated and withdrew.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 13; en.wikipedia Muslim conquest of Persia; Battle of Kaskar
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Firaz
label: Firaz
war: Arab conquest of Persia (Khalid ibn al-Walid in Iraq)
place: Firaz, on the Euphrates between al-Qa'im and Abu Kamal, Syria
commanders_b: not named (Hormozd Jadhuyih on the Persian side according to some accounts)
persian_force: At most a small body of Persian frontier troops, probably survivors of the earlier defeats, beside the Roman garrison and Christian Arabs (Taghlib, Iyad, Namir).
iranian_note: Modern writers doubt that any organised Persian force was present.
result_basis: In the Arabic accounts Khalid routed the coalition after it crossed the Euphrates and held the field.
borderline: Persian participation disputed
doubt: Borderline: Persian participation disputed.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 12 (Sayf ibn Umar); Morony 1984; Crawford 2013; en.wikipedia Battle of Firaz
note: Also in Battles of the Romans as an Arab victory over Rome and the Sasanians. en.wikipedia calls the result disputed; Takirtakoglou suspects the tradition hides a check to Khalid.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Kaskar
label: Kaskar
commanders_a: Abu Ubayd al-Thaqafi, Arfaja ibn Harthama
persian_force: Narsi's own forces defending his estates, with Bindoe's sons Vinduyih and Tiruyih commanding the wings.
iranian_note: A Sasanian prince's household and provincial troops.
result_basis: Narsi's army was defeated before Jalinus could join it; Narsi escaped and his estate was plundered.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 13; en.wikipedia Battle of Kaskar
note: Called al-Saqatiyya in the Arabic sources; en.wikipedia's list has 'Battle of Kaskar' and 'Battle of Saqatia' as two items, but they are one battle.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Namaraq
label: Namaraq
date: 634 (summer or early autumn, before the Bridge)
place: the plain of al-Namariq, near Kufa, Iraq
commanders_a: Abu Ubayd al-Thaqafi, al-Muthanna ibn Haritha
persian_force: Jaban's army sent by Rostam Farrokhzad to retake al-Hira: heavy cavalry and infantry with experienced Persian officers.
iranian_note: A Persian field army raised by Rostam's regency.
result_basis: Jaban was captured and his army retreated, leaving the field to Abu Ubayd.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 13; en.wikipedia Battle of Namaraq
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Babylon (634)
label: Babylon (634)
date: June - July 634 (Tabari dates it to the reign of Shahrbaraz)
persian_force: Hormozd Jadhuyih's army of about 10,000 with a war elephant (al-Tabari).
iranian_note: A Persian field army sent from the capital.
result_basis: Al-Muthanna defeated Hormozd Jadhuyih's army near Babylon and pursued it towards Ctesiphon.
sources: al-Tabari i.2116-2117; en.wikipedia List of battles involving the Rashidun Caliphate ('1st Battle of Babylon')
note: The chronology is confused: Tabari places it under Shahrbaraz (630).
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Bridge
label: Bridge
place: Quss al-Natif on the Euphrates, near Kufa, Iraq
commanders_b: Abu Ubayd al-Thaqafi (killed), al-Muthanna ibn Haritha (wounded)
persian_force: Bahman Jadhuyih's army with about 20 war elephants, heavy cavalry and a deep infantry line.
iranian_note: A Persian field army from the capital; the elephant corps was normally crewed by Indians.
result_basis: The Persian elephants and line broke the Arabs who had crossed the bridge; Abu Ubayd was killed and his army fled back over the river with heavy losses.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 13; Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan; en.wikipedia Battle of the Bridge
note: The only major Sasanian victory over the Arab invaders.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Buwaib
label: Buwaib
date: 635 (April or November 635 in en.wikipedia; Ramadan AH 13 or 14)
place: al-Buwayb, on the Euphrates north of al-Hira (near Kufa), Iraq
persian_force: Mihran's large Persian army sent after the victory at the Bridge (no breakdown in the sources).
iranian_note: A Persian field army from the capital.
result_basis: Al-Muthanna let the Persians cross the river, encircled them and killed Mihran; the Persian army was routed.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 13 (Sayf ibn Umar); Donner 1981; en.wikipedia Battle of Buwaib
note: Local Christian Arabs (Namir, Taghlib) fought for the Muslims. Donner regards the account as unreliable. Dated 634 in many older works.
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Qadisiyyah
label: Qadisiyyah
commanders_a: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Khalid ibn Urfuta, al-Qa'qa' ibn Amr, Zuhra ibn al-Hawiyya, Jarir ibn Abd Allah, Tulayha, Amr ibn Ma'dikarib
commanders_b: Rostam Farrokhzad (killed), Bahman Jadhuyih (killed), Jalinus, Hormuzan, Mihran Razi, Piruz Khosrow, Shahriyar ibn Kanara (killed); Armenian princes Mushegh III Mamikonian and Grigor Novirak (killed); Juansher of Albania (wounded)
persian_force: Rostam's imperial army, about 60,000 (modern estimate about 30,000): heavy cavalry (asawaran), infantry including the Daylamite guard (later the Hamra'), Armenian and Albanian princely contingents, and about 30 elephants.
iranian_note: Persian and Parthian cavalry with Daylamite foot (4,000 of whom went over to the Arabs afterwards), and named Armenian and Albanian princes with their retinues.
result_basis: On the fourth day Rostam was killed and the Persian army broke and fled, leaving the field to the Arabs.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 14 (Sayf ibn Umar); Baladhuri, Futuh al-Buldan; Sebeos 42; Kennedy 2007; en.wikipedia Battle of al-Qadisiyyah
note: The date is disputed (Donner and others prefer 636 or 637; some 638).
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Babylon (636)
label: Babylon (636)
commanders_b: Piruz Khosrow (Firuzan), Hormuzan, Mihran Razi, Nakhiragan
persian_force: The Persian survivors of Qadisiyyah regrouped under Firuzan, Hormuzan, Mihran and Nakhiragan.
iranian_note: The remnant of the imperial army.
result_basis: The Persian commanders gave way before Sa'd's army and withdrew, and Babylon submitted.
borderline: some accounts describe a Persian withdrawal without a real battle
doubt: Borderline: some accounts describe a Persian withdrawal without a real battle.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 16 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Siege of Ctesiphon (637); List of battles involving the Rashidun Caliphate ('2nd Battle of Babylon')
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Burs
label: Burs
persian_force: The Persian garrison of Burs.
iranian_note: A Sasanian garrison of the Sawad.
result_basis: Zuhra killed the garrison commander Busbuhra in single combat and the garrison gave way.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 16 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia Battle of Burs
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Sura
label: Sura
place: Sura, on the Euphrates near Hillah, Iraq
persian_force: A rearguard of the retreating Persian army.
iranian_note: Part of the remnant of the imperial army.
result_basis: Zuhra's vanguard drove off the Persian rearguard at Sura.
borderline: a pursuit skirmish known only from Sayf ibn Umar
doubt: Borderline: a pursuit skirmish known only from Sayf ibn Umar.
sources: al-Tabari, AH 16 (Sayf ibn Umar); en.wikipedia List of battles involving the Rashidun Caliphate
qbasis: Sasanian Empire: an Iranian-led state

name: Hormizd-Ardashir (637)
label: Hormizd-Ardashir (637)
